questions.question: What is another name for front-end header boards?
questions.explanation: Front-end header boards are called headache racks. They protect the driver from cargo that moves forward during a crash or sudden stop.

questions.question: If you discover while driving that your vehicle's ABS is not working, what should you do?

options.text: Use your parking brake to stop.

questions.explanation: If your ABS stops working, your regular brakes still work. Continue to drive and brake normally.

questions.question: Which one is NOT a distracted person that motorists should worry about?

options.text: A driver talking to a passenger in their vehicle
A child on the side of the road
A construction worker on the side of the road
A person sitting on a bench waiting for a bus

questions.correctAnswerText: A person sitting on a bench waiting for a bus
questions.explanation: Be careful around people who are not paying attention to traffic. Watch for distracted drivers, children near the road, and road workers. A person sitting on a bench is not a driving concern.

questions.question: If one air system in a dual air brake system loses pressure:

options.text: None of the brakes will work.
Either the front or rear brakes will not work fully.
There will be no noticeable effect.
Lights on the outside of the tractor will flash.

questions.correctAnswerText: Either the front or rear brakes will not work fully.
questions.explanation: In a dual air brake system, if one air system loses pressure, either the front or rear brakes will not work fully. Stop safely and have the air system fixed.

questions.question: Who is responsible for the safety of loaded cargo?

options.text: A second person can load it and is responsible for its safety.
A second person can load it, but the driver is responsible for its safety.
The shipping company must load it.

questions.correctAnswerText: A second person can load it, but the driver is responsible for its safety.
questions.explanation: The driver is always responsible for the safety of the cargo, no matter who loads it.

questions.question: When traveling downhill, when should you shift to a lower gear?

options.text: As you go downhill and speed up.
Near the bottom of the hill.

questions.explanation: Always shift to a lower gear before you start going downhill. This prevents transmission damage and lets your engine help slow the vehicle. Choose a safe speed based on the hill's steepness, length, your vehicle's weight, road conditions, and weather.

questions.question: Which one is NOT required equipment on a commercial vehicle?

options.text: Warning devices for parked vehicles, such as flares.

questions.explanation: Commercial vehicles must have a fire extinguisher, spare fuses (unless the vehicle has circuit breakers), and warning devices like triangles or flares. A spotlight is not required.

questions.question: What should you do when using turn signals?

options.text: It is best to hide your intentions from others.
Only use them if other vehicles are nearby.
Do not use them in construction zones.
Always use them to tell others what you plan to do.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always use them to tell others what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: Always signal before turning or changing lanes. This tells other drivers what you are doing, even if no other vehicles are nearby.

questions.question: When do spring brakes come on?

options.text: When air pressure gets too low.
When you press a dashboard button.
When your tires have little tread.

questions.correctAnswerText: When air pressure gets too low.
questions.explanation: Spring brakes come on automatically when air pressure drops too low. Do not wait for this to happen. Stop safely as soon as you see the low pressure warning light.

questions.question: An air brake vehicle traveling at 55 mph in ideal conditions needs approximately how many feet to stop?
questions.explanation: Stopping distance includes perception time, reaction time, brake lag, and actual braking. An air brake vehicle at 55 mph in ideal conditions needs about 450 feet to stop completely.

questions.question: You see lights ahead while driving in fog. What should you know?

options.text: The lights are definitely on the road.
The lights may be a reflection.
The lights may be an optical illusion.
The lights may not show where the road actually is. The vehicle may have left the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lights may not show where the road actually is. The vehicle may have left the road.
questions.explanation: In fog, lights are not a reliable guide for where the road is. The lights could come from a vehicle that has left the roadway.

questions.question: At what air pressure will an air compressor governor stop pumping?
questions.explanation: The air compressor governor stops pumping when the air tanks reach 125 psi. This is called the "cut-out" level.

questions.question: What is true about driving too fast?

options.text: It is a major cause of fatal crashes.
It is a good way to reach your destination quickly.
It is okay if the road is dry.
It is acceptable when traffic is light.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is a major cause of fatal crashes.
questions.explanation: Speeding is a major cause of fatal crashes. Never drive above the speed limit. Adjust your speed to match the road and weather conditions.

questions.question: You are unsure if your vehicle can safely fit under a bridge. What should you do?

options.text: Swerve as you pass under the bridge.

questions.explanation: If you are not sure your vehicle will fit under a bridge, slow down and find another route if possible.

questions.question: How can a driver check if the road is becoming icy?

options.text: Open the window and check the side mirror for ice.

questions.correctAnswerText: Open the window and check the side mirror for ice.
questions.explanation: Open your window and touch the side mirror, mirror support, or antenna. If ice has formed on these items, the road surface is likely becoming icy too.

questions.question: When should mirror adjustment be checked?

options.text: Only if the driver plans to use the mirrors.

questions.explanation: Check and adjust your mirrors before you start every trip.

questions.question: What is the minimum size for a hazardous materials placard?
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials placards must be diamond-shaped and at least 10 ¾ square inches in size.

questions.question: An aggressive driver is confronting you. What should you do?

options.text: Make eye contact with the driver.
Challenge the driver to a race.

questions.explanation: If you encounter an aggressive driver, get out of their way if you can. Do not make eye contact, challenge them, or react to their gestures.

questions.question: Your tire fails while driving. What should you do?

options.text: Wave your arms at other drivers.

questions.explanation: Using the brakes after a tire fails can cause you to lose control. Stay off the brakes unless you are about to hit something. Let the vehicle slow down on its own.

questions.question: What do slippery roadways usually do?

options.text: Make it harder to stop a vehicle.
Make it easier to stop a vehicle.
Make it easier to drive a vehicle.
Can be avoided by driving at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make it harder to stop a vehicle.
questions.explanation: It takes longer to stop on a slippery road than on a dry road. Be extra careful when driving on roads that are or could become slippery.

questions.question: Cargo that is 40 feet long on a flatbed trailer must be secured with at least:
questions.explanation: On flatbed trailers, cargo must be tied down. Use at least one tie-down for every 10 feet of cargo. Always use at least two tie-downs, no matter how small the cargo is.

questions.question: When checking your mirrors, you should:

options.text: Not use the passenger side mirror.
Not use the driver's side mirror.
Look in each mirror for a long time.

questions.explanation: To drive safely, you need to know what is happening on all sides of your vehicle at all times. Check both mirrors often while driving.

questions.question: An open car window in cold weather may mean the driver is:

options.text: Using the heat in the vehicle.

questions.explanation: Watch other drivers for signs they may be impaired. Drivers who have drunk too much, are tired, are using drugs, or are sick can be dangerous. An open window in cold weather is one sign of an impaired driver.

questions.question: At highway speeds, you should look ahead about ____ on the road.
questions.explanation: Watch the road 12 to 15 seconds ahead of your vehicle to spot hazards early. At highway speeds, this is about a quarter mile ahead.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT an example of a hazardous driver?

options.text: A driver who doesn't scrape ice off the windshield
A driver of a station wagon with items blocking the back windows
A person driving a pick-up truck

questions.correctAnswerText: A person driving a pick-up truck
questions.explanation: Drivers with blocked vision are hazardous. Examples include drivers with ice on windshields, drivers with large items blocking windows, and those unfamiliar with rental trucks that have poor rear visibility.

questions.question: Cargo that doesn't fill the entire trailer should be placed:

options.text: At the front of the trailer.
At the rear of the trailer.
In the middle of the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the middle of the trailer.
questions.explanation: Balance cargo so weight is even on the front and rear axles. Unbalanced cargo can damage a vehicle and cause poor handling.

questions.question: ____ is a thin, clear layer of ice on road surfaces.
questions.explanation: Black ice is a thin, clear layer of ice on the road. You can see the road through it, so it looks like the road is just wet.

questions.question: Poisonous fumes can enter a truck cab because of:

options.text: Not enough oil in the engine.

questions.explanation: A broken exhaust system is dangerous because poisonous fumes can enter the cab or sleeper berth.

questions.question: Why are roads extra slippery when rain first begins to fall?

options.text: The water mixes with oil and grease on the road.
Gravel gets washed to the middle of the lane.
Tires are not made for rain.

questions.correctAnswerText: The water mixes with oil and grease on the road.
questions.explanation: Roads are most slippery when rain first starts. Fresh rainwater mixes with oil and grease on the road to create a slick film. As rain continues, this mixture washes away.

questions.question: A modulating control valve controls the:
questions.explanation: A modulating control valve lets a driver slowly apply spring brakes. The valve is controlled by a lever on the dashboard in equipped vehicles.

questions.question: When starting the engine during a pre-trip inspection, what should the driver do?
questions.explanation: During a pre-trip inspection, start the engine and listen for any strange sounds.

questions.question: Before driving a vehicle with a dual brake system, what should a driver do?

options.text: Let the vehicle warm up to ensure fuel reaches the engine.
Wait for air pressure to build in both the primary and secondary systems.
Begin driving right after the engine starts.
Pump the pedal about 20 times to build pressure, then start driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for air pressure to build in both the primary and secondary systems.
questions.explanation: Before driving a vehicle with a dual air brake system, let the compressor build air pressure to at least 100 psi in both systems.

questions.question: In cold weather, how often should an alcohol evaporator be checked and filled?
questions.explanation: An alcohol evaporator prevents ice from building up in an air brake system. In cold weather, check and refill it every day.

questions.question: When crossing railroad tracks, what should you do?
questions.explanation: When crossing railroad tracks, do not stop, change gears, pass another vehicle, or change lanes while any part of your vehicle is on the tracks.

questions.question: What is true about vehicles with dual air brake systems?

options.text: They keep full air pressure in the braking systems even when the engine is off.
They keep some air pressure in the braking systems when the engine is off.
They must run to build enough air pressure for the brakes to work properly.
They do not need time to build air pressure before driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: They must run to build enough air pressure for the brakes to work properly.
questions.explanation: Before driving a vehicle with a dual air brake system, you must let the air compressor build at least 100 psi of pressure in both the primary and secondary systems.

questions.question: A vehicle must have all of the following equipment, except:

options.text: Warning devices for a parked vehicle.

questions.explanation: Commercial vehicles must have emergency equipment. This includes spare electrical fuses, warning devices (reflective triangles, flares, or fuses), and a fire extinguisher.

questions.question: An Individual Vehicle Distance Record (IVDR) must include all of the following, except:
questions.explanation: An IVDR must include the trip start and end dates, origin and destination, route, odometer readings, total distance, in-jurisdiction distance, and vehicle identification number. It does not need to include the number of stops.

questions.question: What is rough acceleration?

options.text: Is necessary to warm up the engine.
Is encouraged to improve gas mileage.
Should be done on surfaces with poor traction.

questions.explanation: Accelerate smoothly and gradually. Rough acceleration can cause mechanical damage to the vehicle.

questions.question: What can help you decide when to shift to a higher gear?
questions.explanation: Two things help you know when to shift up. First, watch engine speed (rpm). Check your vehicle manual for the correct rpm range and shift up when you reach the top. Second, watch road speed (mph). Learn which speeds work with each gear and use your speedometer to shift up when needed.

questions.question: What is a concern right when it starts to rain?

options.text: Water mixes with grease and oil on the road, making it slippery.
A driver may forget where the windshield wiper lever is.
People will use their windshield wipers too much.

questions.correctAnswerText: Water mixes with grease and oil on the road, making it slippery.
questions.explanation: Roads are most slippery when rain first starts. The water mixes with oil and grease on the road before it washes away.

questions.question: What is black ice?

options.text: A thick layer of ice on the road
A thin layer of ice on the road
Ice that is black because of dirt on the road
Ice that is easy to see

questions.correctAnswerText: A thin layer of ice on the road
questions.explanation: Black ice is a thin, clear layer of ice. You can see the road through it. A road with black ice looks wet, not icy.

questions.question: If a car pulls out in front of you and you cannot stop, you should:

options.text: Hit the other vehicle since it is the other driver's fault
Swerve to avoid the other car

questions.correctAnswerText: Swerve to avoid the other car
questions.explanation: Try to brake first if you have room to stop. If you do not have room to stop, swerving is a safer choice than hitting the other vehicle.

questions.question: A one-way check valve:

options.text: Drains water and compressor oil from the air tanks
Stops air from escaping if the air compressor leaks
Activates the emergency brakes when there is a leak
Holds the spring brakes in place until they are used

questions.correctAnswerText: Stops air from escaping if the air compressor leaks
questions.explanation: A one-way check valve is placed between the air compressor and the first main tank. It prevents air from escaping the system if the compressor leaks.

questions.question: When using a fire extinguisher on a fire, you should:

options.text: Get as close to the fire as possible
Stay as far away from the fire as possible
Aim at the top of the flames
Aim at the ground about two feet away from the fire

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay as far away from the fire as possible
questions.explanation: Stay as far away from the flames as possible. Aim at the base of the fire, not the top.

questions.question: A commercial vehicle should:

options.text: Have a fire extinguisher only if carrying hazardous materials
Have a fire extinguisher only if traveling through remote areas
Have a fire extinguisher and other emergency equipment

questions.correctAnswerText: Have a fire extinguisher and other emergency equipment
questions.explanation: All commercial vehicles must have proper emergency equipment. This includes spare fuses, three red reflective triangles or flares, and at least one working fire extinguisher.

questions.question: When driving with covered cargo, a flapping cover:
questions.explanation: Cargo covers should not flap. They can tear loose, which uncovers the cargo and blocks other drivers' views.

questions.question: What do headers do?

options.text: Protect the driver during a crash

questions.correctAnswerText: Protect the driver during a crash
questions.explanation: Header boards on the front of a vehicle protect the driver if cargo moves forward during a crash or sudden stop.

questions.question: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) uses a ____ light to show the system is not working.
questions.explanation: ABS warning lights are usually yellow. Even if ABS fails, the regular brakes will still work.

questions.question: Brake fading happens when:

options.text: Brakes are not used often enough

questions.explanation: Heavy brake use causes them to overheat and become less effective. This is called "fading."

questions.question: The front of an enclosed trailer should:
questions.explanation: When inspecting an enclosed trailer, check the front for damage such as cracks, bulges, or holes.
